edges.description: Mutant receptors fail to generate cGMP in response to CNP and, for dominant-negative alleles, also suppress the wild-type receptor. This leaves heterozygotes with less than normal NPR-B output.
CNP/cGMP signalling normally restrains FGF-driven ERK activation in chondrocytes. Less NPR-B output weakens that brake, which reduces chondrocyte differentiation and hypertrophy.
intermediate_mechanisms: Reduced cGMP-dependent restraint of FGF-induced ERK1/2 activation

edges.description: Fewer and less fully differentiated hypertrophic chondrocytes limit longitudinal elongation of endochondral bones.
Reduced longitudinal bone growth directly lowers attained height.
Because the growth deficit acts throughout childhood, the height SDS of heterozygous children falls as they grow.
Limb growth is affected somewhat more than trunk growth in some patients, giving mild disproportion.
Reduced growth of short tubular bones of the hand gives short metacarpals.
Altered growth of the phalanges can give finger clinodactyly.
Reduced prenatal longitudinal growth can show as small-for-gestational-age birth length in some heterozygotes.
Npr2 loss shrinks the proliferative and hypertrophic zones of the growth plate and raises activated ERK1/2 in the tibia, the chondrocyte deficit this node describes.
edges.limitations: Homozygous null rather than heterozygous, so the deficit is far larger than in patients with one variant allele; the model says nothing about the dominant-negative alleles some heterozygotes carry.

edges.description: MEK1/2 inhibitors restore growth of cultured fetal mutant tibiae, placing ERK disinhibition between Npr2 loss and the bone-growth deficit.
edges.limitations: The rescue was shown in fetal tibia explants, not in living animals or postnatal bone, and in a homozygous null rather than a heterozygous model.

edges.description: A catalytic-domain missense allele leaves chondrocytes unable to raise cGMP in response to CNP.
edges.limitations: Homozygous, so cGMP output is absent rather than reduced. The measurement was made in cultured chondrocytes from the mice and in transfected COS-7 cells, not in the growth plate in vivo.

edges.description: cn/cn mice have disproportionate dwarfism with short limbs and tail from disturbed chondrogenesis during endochondral ossification, the bone-growth outcome of the cGMP deficit this model also shows.
edges.limitations: Homozygous, so the growth failure is a dysplasia rather than the mild short stature of heterozygous patients.

edges.description: Loss of GC-B impairs endochondral ossification and longitudinal vertebral and limb-bone growth.
edges.limitations: Complete null, so growth failure is far more severe than in heterozygous patients; the female infertility of null mice has no counterpart in this entry.

edges.description: Null mice lack GC-B entirely, and the authors attribute the endochondral-ossification defect to loss of CNP-stimulated rather than basal GC-B activity, the quantity this node describes.
edges.limitations: The abstract states that CNP-stimulated activity "appeared to be required"; it does not report a cGMP measurement in growth-plate chondrocytes, so this link rests on the authors' inference. A complete null removes the receptor rather than reducing its output, and cannot represent the dominant-negative alleles some heterozygous patients carry.

nodes.description: Finger clinodactyly is reported as a minor hand finding.

nodes.description: In growth-plate chondrocytes, reduced NPR-B signalling impairs differentiation toward the hypertrophic state. Some misfolded mutant receptors also add endoplasmic-reticulum stress and chondrocyte apoptosis.

nodes.description: A single pathogenic NPR2 allele, germline and frequently inherited from a similarly short parent, initiates the disease. Allele classes include missense, splice-site and truncating variants spread across the ligand-binding, kinase-homology and guanylyl-cyclase domains.

evidence.snippet: Of these variants, 5 were truncating, 11 were non-truncating, and 2 were splice site. Most were located in the ligand binding domain or kinase homology domain (KHD).

nodes.description: Mild limb-trunk disproportion is common in clinic and registry cohorts. Some patients resemble Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis without Madelung deformity. Family-based studies have also reported proportionate short stature, so disproportion is not required.

evidence.snippet: C-type natriuretic peptide-dependent increases of guanylyl cyclase B activity, but not basal enzyme activity, appeared to be required for the progression of endochondral ossification.

nodes.description: A spontaneous recessive achondroplastic mouse with disproportionate dwarfism, short limbs and tail. Its Npr2 missense allele abolishes CNP-stimulated cGMP production, the molecular step this entry's mechanism starts from.

evidence.reference_title: A loss-of-function mutation in natriuretic peptide receptor 2 (Npr2) gene is responsible for disproportionate dwarfism in cn/cn mouse.
evidence.snippet: The achondroplastic mouse is a spontaneous mutant characterized by disproportionate dwarfism with short limbs and tail due to disturbed chondrogenesis during endochondral ossification.

nodes.description: A recessive loss-of-function Npr2 allele that models acromesomelic dysplasia, Maroteaux type. It shows the growth-plate consequence of losing NPR-B signalling and the ERK disinhibition behind it. Because it is biallelic, it bears on the mechanism of the heterozygous disease but not on its size.

evidence.reference_title: A novel loss-of-function mutation in Npr2 clarifies primary role in female reproduction and reveals a potential therapy for acromesomelic dysplasia, Maroteaux type.
evidence.snippet: The Npr2(pwe/pwe) mouse is a model for the human skeletal dysplasia acromesomelic dysplasia, Maroteaux type (AMDM).

nodes.description: Height SDS declines as heterozygous children grow, so the deficit is often more marked at older ages than in early childhood.

evidence.reference_title: Short Stature is Progressive in Patients with Heterozygous NPR2 Mutations.
evidence.snippet: Height z-scores progressively and significantly decreased as NPR2-heterozygous children matured, while remaining constant in their wild-type siblings.

nodes.description: NPR-B is a homodimeric receptor guanylyl cyclase. Heterozygous variants lower CNP-stimulated cGMP output by three routes: loss of one functional allele (haploinsufficiency); retention of misfolded receptor in the endoplasmic reticulum; or dominant-negative poisoning of wild-type subunits by catalytically dead mutant receptors that still reach the cell surface. The route varies by allele.

nodes.description: Recombinant human growth hormone is widely used, often under idiopathic or SGA short-stature indications. Early reports described little response. Larger cohorts report height gains, greater in prepubertal than in pubertal children, with variable individual response. No controlled trial in this disease has been reported.

evidence.snippet: After 2 years of GH treatment, median height gain SDS in prepubertal children was 1.2 (0.8 to 1.4) and in pubertal children 0.5 (0.3 to 0.9).

evidence.snippet: The growth velocity in the first year of GH treatment accelerated by 3.6 to 4.2 cm/year; the height improved by 1.2 to 1.8 SD over 5 years of treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Heterozygous NPR2 Variants in Idiopathic Short Stature.

nodes.description: Vosoritide is a CNP analogue approved for achondroplasia. In a phase 2 open-label basket trial (NCT04219007) it increased annualized growth velocity in children with heterozygous NPR2 deficiency among other genetic short stature groups. It is investigational for this indication. Slipped capital femoral epiphysis and genu valgum were seen in the basket trial but not in the NPR2 subgroup.

evidence.reference_title: A phase II basket trial of vosoritide in children with RASopathies, ACAN, and NPR2 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The increase in AGV was seen in all genetic subgroups.

evidence.reference_title: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis during Vosoritide Therapy for Short Stature: A Case Series.
evidence.snippet: In the basket trial, SCFE was observed in 2/12 participants with ACAN mutations, 1/11 with RASopathy but not in the 7 participants with NPR2 mutations or 24 with hypochondroplasia.
